name: Martial Master
body:
The martial master focuses their training on a few weapons and becomes so adept at their use that the combat forms become innate movements. They also use their calm and focus to enter a state of fluid battle meditation in the midst of the chaos of combat. This allows them to react and perform feats not normally seen by their weapon-wielding peers.

Hybrid Class: The martial master is a hybrid of the barbarian, monk and swashbuckler classes.

Role: The martial master is a combatant that uses their battle meditation to focus their melee or ranged combat. The reduced proficiency gained by the martial master forces them to focus a bit more on a combat style but they can equally fill a melee role as a ranged one.

Alignment: Any. Martial masters can be of any alignment. That said, martial masters with their need for mental focus and control tend toward lawful.

Hit Die: d8

Starting Wealth: 4d6 × 10 gp (average 140 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The martial master’s class skills are: Acrobatics (Dex), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (local) (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Points Per Level: 4 + Intelligence Modifier

Level	Base Attack Bonus	Fort Save	Ref Save	Will Save	Class Features
1st	+1	+0	+2	+2	Battle meditation, focus, focus technique, intuitive skill, martial defense, weapon experience
2nd	+2	+0	+3	+3	Combat awareness, focus technique, uncanny dodge
3rd	+3	+1	+3	+3	Weapon training
4th	+4	+1	+4	+4	Bonus feat, focus technique
5th	+5	+1	+4	+4	Improved uncanny dodge, weapon experience
6th	+6/+1	+2	+5	+5	Focus technique, instant readiness
7th	+7/+2	+2	+5	+5	Weapon Training
8th	+8/+3	+2	+6	+6	Bonus feat, focus technique
9th	+9/+4	+3	+6	+6	Recenter the mind
10th	+10/+5	+3	+7	+7	Focus technique, weapon experience
11th	+11/+6/+1	+3	+7	+7	Weapon Training
12th	+12/+7/+2	+4	+8	+8	Bonus feat, focus technique
13th	+13/+8/+3	+4	+8	+8	Heightened battle meditation
14th	+14/+9/+4	+4	+9	+9	Focus technique
15th	+15/+10/+5	+5	+9	+9	Weapon experience, weapon training
16th	+16/+11/+6/+1	+5	+10	+10	Bonus feat, focus technique
17th	+17/+12/+7/+2	+5	+10	+10	Mental preparation, unbreakable focus
18th	+18/+13/+8/+3	+6	+11	+11	Focus technique
19th	+19/+14/+9/+4	+6	+11	+11	Weapon training
20th	+20/+15/+10/+5	+6	+12	+12	Bonus feat, focus technique, master of masters
Class Features

The following are the class features of the martial master.

Weapon Expertise

A martial master is skilled in the usage of a set of weapons. At 1st level, a martial master chooses two weapon sets from the fighter weapon groups. They gain proficiency with all the weapons of that weapon group. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter (except for 20th level), they gain proficiency with another weapon group. If the weapon group selected includes unarmed strikes, the martial master gains Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat. If the weapon group includes shields, you gain proficiency with all shields except for tower shields.

Martial Defense

A martial master, though focused on weapon skill, must defend themselves. At 1st level, the martial master must choose between armored defense or unfettered defense. Once the choice is made, it cannot be changed later. If the martial master chooses armored defense, they gain proficiency with all armor and shields, including tower shields. If the martial master chooses unfettered defense, while they are unarmored and have no more than a medium load, they may add their Wisdom bonus (if any) to their AC and CMD. In addition, the martial master gains a +1 bonus to AC and CMD at 4th level. This bonus increases by 1 for every four levels thereafter, up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level.

These unfettered AC bonuses apply even against touch attacks or when the martial master is flat-footed. They lose these bonuses if they are immobilized or helpless, when they wear armor, when wielding a shield (unless included in a weapon group from your weapon expertise), or carrying a heavy load.

Focus (Ex)

The crux of the martial master’s skill is their ability to center their mind and focus on their technique in the heat of combat. At 1st level, the martial master gains a number of Focus points (FP) equal to 1/2 their martial master level + their Wisdom modifier (min. 1). These Focus points is replenished after 8 hours of rest or meditation; these hours do not need to be consecutive.

Battle Meditation

The martial master can enter a state of meditation that further enhances their combat focus. At 1st level, the martial master may enter the state of battle meditation for 1 minute by expending 1 point of Focus as a free action.

The battle meditation gives clarity to the martial master granting them a +4 bonus to Wisdom and a +2 bonus on saves vs. spells or effects with the emotion descriptor. They may also use their Wisdom modifier instead of the Dexterity modifier for Reflex saves.

Additionally, while in battle meditation, any weapon they are proficient with deals the higher of their normal damage die or the damage die listed on the table below, determined by their class level.

A martial master may end their battle meditation as a free action. If the martial master may not resume battle meditation until a number of rounds equal to the rounds spent in battle meditation previously have passed. Otherwise, the martial master may enter battle meditation multiple times during a single encounter or combat. If the martial master falls unconscious, their battle meditation immediately ends.

Battle Meditation, Rage and Losing Mental Focus Given the nature of battle meditation as opposed to rage (or abilities similar to rage or effects that induce a rage like state), battle meditation may not be active while such effects are active. If the martial master is subject to the rage spell and fails their saving throw, battle meditation immediately ends. Also, if the martial master is under the effects of a spell or ability that induces strong negative emotions, like crushing despair or spells and effects that cause loss of mental focus like a bard’s fascinate they may not activate battle meditation and their battle meditation immediately ends.

Focus Techniques (Ex)

As a martial master gains levels, they learn new techniques to employ while in their battle meditation. Starting at 1st level, a martial master gains a focus technique. They gain another focus technique at 2nd level and every two levels thereafter. The focus techniques have a Focus point (FP) cost listed in the title of the focus technique along with the minimum level required. If the martial master is in their battle meditation, the Focus point cost for the technique is reduced by 1. Unless otherwise noted, the martial master cannot select an individual technique more than once. Finally, focus techniques can only be used with weapons from weapon groups chosen with weapon expertise.

Level	Damage Dice (M)	Damage Dice (S)
1st-4th	1d6	1d4
5th-9th	1d8	1d6
10th-14th	1d10	1d8
15th-19th	2d6	1d10
20th	2d8	2d6
Intuitive Skill (Ex)

At 1st level, the martial master uses their focus and intuition to help them with their techniques. They use their Wisdom in place of Intelligence for combat feat prerequisites.

Combat Awareness (Ex)

At 2nd level, if the martial master is in a state of battle meditation, they know the current hit point total of each adjacent opponent and ally. This ability does not work if the creature is invisible until 7th level or later. At 7th level, the martial master also gains blindsense out to 5 feet. At 17th level, this blindsense becomes blindsight.

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 2nd level, a martial master gains the ability to react to danger before their senses would normally allow them to do so. They cannot be caught flat-footed, nor do they lose their Dexterity bonus to armor class if the attacker is invisible. They still lose their Dexterity bonus to armor class if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against them. If the martial master already has uncanny dodge from a different class, they automatically gain improved uncanny dodge (see below) instead.

Weapon Training (Ex)

At 3rd level, a martial master can select one of the groups of weapons chosen with weapon experience. Whenever they attack with a weapon from that group, they gain a +1 bonus on attack, CMB, CMD vs. disarm and sunder, and damage rolls. Additionally, when using any weapon from the selected group, the martial master may use their Wisdom modifier in lieu of their Strength or Dexterity on attack rolls and damage rolls.

At 7th level and every four levels thereafter (11th, 15th, and 19th), the bonuses to attack and damage provided to weapons in the selected weapon group(s) increases by 1.

At each of those levels, the martial master may choose another weapon group to apply their weapon training bonus to or gain an advanced weapon training (using their martial master level as their fighter level).

This ability acts as and stacks with a fighter’s weapon training.

Bonus Feats

At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, a martial master gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement. These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as combat feats.

Martial master levels are considered fighter levels for the purposes of meeting combat feat prerequisites. In addition, upon reaching 8th level and every 4 levels thereafter, a martial master can choose to learn a new bonus feat in place of a bonus feat they have already learned. In effect, the martial master loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. The old feat cannot be one that was used as a prerequisite for another feat, prestige class, or other ability. A martial master can only change one feat at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the feat at the time they gain a new bonus feat for the level.

Improved Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 5th level and higher, a martial master can no longer be flanked. This defense denies a rogue the ability to sneak attack the martial master unless the attacker has at least four more rogue levels than the target has martial master levels. If a character already has uncanny dodge (see above) from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum rogue level required to flank the character.

Instant Readiness (Ex)

Danger is always at hand and the martial master understands this. Starting at 6th level, a martial master may choose to enter their battle meditation when rolling for initiative.

Recenter the Mind (Ex)

At 9th level, the martial master has learned to enter a meditative state to refresh their mind and sharpen their focus. They may take 10 minutes to meditate. At the end of the 10 minutes, the martial master regains 1 Focus point. While meditating, the martial master must close themselves off to external stimuli and remain motionless for the entire duration. They are considered unconscious for the duration though they may be roused from their state by an ally taking a move action to awaken them. If the 10 minutes is interrupted, the benefits are lost.

Heightened Battle Meditation (Ex)

At 13th level, when the martial master enters their battle meditation, the bonus to Wisdom increases to +6 and their bonus to saves vs. spells or effects with the emotion descriptor increases to +3 and the bonus also applies to all mind- affecting spells or effects.

Mental Preparation (Ex)

At 17th level, the martial master has gained the ability to exit and enter their battle meditation with ease. They no longer need to wait between uses of their battle meditation.

Unbreakable Focus (Ex)

At 17th level, when the martial master is in their battle meditation, they are immune to all mind-affecting spells or effects. They may choose to lower this immunity at will.

Master of Masters (Ex)

At 20th level, the martial master is at the peak of their art. Their reputation and skill is known far and wide. Any other character of a martial class (like fighter, ranger martial master, etc.) always has a minimum attitude of indifferent to the martial master unless they have been given direct orders to oppose them. The martial master need no longer spend a point of Focus to enter battle meditation. Additionally, they become proficient with all weapons and the bonus to Wisdom provided by battle meditation increases to +8.

Focus Techniques

Ammo Threat (Ex) (1 FP, 8th): When wielding a ranged weapon, the martial master threatens attacks of opportunity with their ranged weapon as if they were wielding a non-reach melee weapon. Each attack of opportunity made in this way uses a focus point, if applicable. The martial master must have the guarded shots focus technique to gain this technique.

Bleeding Wound (Ex) (2 FP, 6th): When the martial master hits a living creature they can expend the requisite Focus points as a free action to have the attack deal additional bleed damage. The amount of bleed damage dealt is equal to the martial master’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Creatures immune to precision damage are immune to this bleed damage. Starting at 12th level, the martial master can expend 1 additional point of Focus to deal 1 point of Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution bleed damage instead (martial master’s choice).

Deadly Hit (Ex) (2 FP, 18th): When the martial master confirms a critical hit, in addition to normal damage, they can expend Focus to strike a particularly deadly spot. The target must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw or die. The DC of this save is 10 + 1/2 the martial master’s class level + the martial master’s Wisdom modifier. This is a death effect.

Dire Focus (Ex) (1 FP, 18th): The critical threat range for the weapon the martial master wields is increased by 2. This range increase stacks with feats, magic or magic item properties that improve the weapon’s threat range. The enhanced critical threat range may be activated by expending a focus point, if applicable, after the attack is rolled but before the results of the attack are declared.

Drawing Attack (Ex) (1 FP, 1st): The martial master is able to draw and stow a weapon as a free action, no expenditure of Focus points required. Additionally, they may expend Focus, if applicable, to perform a drawing attack. When making an attack while drawing their weapon, they add their martial master level to the damage. This drawing attack can only happen once per round and must be the first attack in a full-attack action, if applicable. This technique counts as the Quickdraw feat for prerequisite purposes. However, any feat that uses this ability as a prerequisite may only be used in conjunction with this ability. If the martial master already has Quickdraw or later gains the feat, they may draw, attack, and stow their weapon in the same attack action.

Extension of the Arm (Su) (2 FP, 8th): The martial master is able to focus their will into a projection from their weapon. They may expend Focus to increase the range of one of their melee attacks to close range (25 feet + 5 ft/2 class levels). This attack deals the normal damage of the weapon and uses their normal melee attack modifiers. This may not be used on attacks of opportunity and does not increase the martial master’s threatened area.

Focused Healing (Su) (2 FP, 1st): The martial master is able to focus their will to heal the wounds of themselves and their allies. The martial master can expend Focus to heal 1d6 damage to themselves as a swift action or to an another as a standard action. This healing increases by 1d6 for every 2 class levels the martial master possesses. The martial master may expend additional Focus to increase the healing by 1d6 per 2 class levels, but each additional set of d6 adds 2 FP to the cost.

Focused Redirection (Ex) (2 FP, 6th): The martial master may expend Focus as an immediate action to regain advantage from a missed attack. They may chose one of the following.

They may to reroll an attack they missed. The attack is made at the same attack bonus as the missing attack but with an additional -2 penalty.
They may deal the minimum damage of their wielded weapon.
They may redirect the attack to another target within range, comparing the original attack roll against the next target’s AC.

Force of Personality (Sp) (2 FP, 2nd): The martial master is able to project their mental will upon another. By expending Focus as a standard action they can attempt to assert mental control over another. The target must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the martial master’s class level + the martial master’s Wisdom modifier). If the target fails, you may impose the sickened, shaken or confused conditions. If the target fails by 5 or more is has HD less than the martial master’s level -4, they may also be affected as per the spell suggestion. The condition imposed lasts for 1 round per level or until the martial master ends it. At 6th level you may also affect the target as if by the spell charm monster. This is a mind-affecting effect.

Force of Will (Su) (2 FP, 4th): The martial master is able to use their sheer force of will to move a target (including objects). As part of an attack action (full or standard) they may replace one of their attacks with a special bull rush combat maneuver. To do so, they must expend Focus as a free action. They may affect any one creature within close range (25 feet + 5 ft/2 class levels). The special bull rush may come from any direction, pushing the target in any direction, as long as the origination point is also within range. For this special bull rush, instead of using their Strength modifier for the maneuver check, they use their Wisdom modifier, all other modifiers and feat effects to the combat maneuver remain the same. If the martial master would trigger an attack of opportunity from their bull rush attempt, this special ability triggers an attack of opportunity as well. At 8th level, your skill refines to allow you to perform a dirty trick or trip combat maneuvers. At 12th level, you can perform a disarm combat maneuver. In all cases, you may apply any feats or abilities normally applied to combat maneuvers you posses to this special combat maneuver.

Flurry (Ex) (1 FP, 1st): The martial master is able to attack with a series of rapid attacks, using battle intuition rather than sight to place them. As part of a full attack action, the martial master may expend Focus, if applicable, to make one additional attack at their highest base attack bonus. All attacks or combat maneuvers made during the attack sequence suffer a -2 penalty. This ability does not stack with other feats or abilities that grant additional attacks but does stack with spell effects like haste or with the speed weapon property.

Guarded Shots (Ex) (1 FP, 2nd): The martial master no longer provokes attacks of opportunity when using a ranged weapon in an attacker’s threatened area. If Focus points are required, they must be expended for each attack of opportunity they wish to negate.

Hidden Blade (Ex) (2 FP, 4th): If you succeed in killing or knocking a target unconscious with a drawing strike. You may expend Focus to quickly sheathe or stow your weapon to hide that you were the attacker. You make a Bluff or Stealth check using your Wisdom in lieu of Charisma or Dexterity against the Perception of any observers, including the target, should they survive. If you succeed, no one would think you were the one who made the attack without obvious other evidence. If further skill checks are needed as part of the ruse like hiding the body or bluffing that you saw another attacker fleeing, you may use your Wisdom in lieu of the normal required stat for the skill check for the next minute.

Infused Weapon (Su) (1 FP, 1st): The martial master’s weapons become infused with a modicum of their will. Any weapon they wield is treated as a magic weapon for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. At 7th level, the weapon is also considered cold iron and silver for this purpose. At 16th level, it instead becomes adamantine. At 10th level, the weapon takes on the non-neutral alignment aspect of the martial master for the purposes of bypassing damage reduction. For example, the weapon of a Lawful Good martial master would be considered both lawful and good for that purpose. If Focus points are required, they may be expended as a free action and lasts for 1 round.

Intuitive Compensation (Ex) (1 FP, 2nd): The martial master can suppress the broken condition from a single weapon they are currently wielding. If Focus point expenditure is required, it is expended as a free action and lasts for 1 round

Intuitive Dodge (Ex) (2 FP, 2nd): Your focus is so keen that you can anticipate the movements of your opponents. When an opponent attempts an attack (physical or magical) against the martial master, they may, as an immediate action, expend Focus to move 5 feet. This movement does not negate the attack, which is still resolved as if the martial master had not moved from the original square but it imposes a 10% miss chance on the original attacker. This movement is not a 5-foot-step; it provokes attacks of opportunity from creatures other than the one that triggered this technique. The miss chance increases by 10% for every 2 levels after 2nd.

Intuitive Evasion (Ex) (1 FP, 8th): The martial master gains the benefits of evasion. At 14th level, this improves to improved evasion. Levels in other classes do not count toward this total. If expending Focus is required, it is used as an immediate action and is per saving throw.

Intuitive Strike (Ex) (2 FP, 4th): As a swift action, a martial master can expend Focus to double their Wisdom bonus to their damage on their attacks for 1 round.

Intuitive Technique (Ex) (1 FP, 1st): The martial master may use their Wisdom modifier in place of the typical modifier for Acrobatics, Bluff, Escape Artist and Sleight of Hand skill checks. If expending Focus is required, it is as a free action per skill check.

Lightness of Being (Su) (1 or 2 FP, 1st): The martial master can focus their will to perform amazing acrobatic feats. The martial master can go from sitting/prone to standing or visa-versa as a move action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If Focus points are required, it is per movement. They may expend an additional point of Focus to make the movement as a swift action.

Additionally, the martial master may expend 2 Focus points (1 in battle meditation) as an immediate action to gain one of the following benefits for one round:

Slow fall of 10 feet per 2 martial master levels.
+10 bonus to Acrobatics checks while jumping.

Menacing Skill (Ex) (1 FP, 1st): When a martial master hits an opponent, they can choose to use Intimidate to demoralize that opponent as a swift action instead of a standard action. A successful combat maneuver is considered a ‘hit’ for this purpose.

This ability may only be used once per round. If focus points are required, they are expended per attempt.

Overwhelming Skill (Ex) (2 FP, 14th): As a swift action, the martial master may expend Focus to project their superior skill to their opponents. All enemies within 60 feet of the martial master must make a Will save (DC equal to 10 + 1/2 the martial master’s class levels + their Wisdom modifier) or become shaken until the end of combat. Any creature that fails its save by 5 or more is frightened. Any enemy with fewer HD than the martial master’s HD – 4 gets no saving throw and is frightened for 1 minute. Afterwards they become shaken for the duration.

Regardless of the outcome, this ability can only affect a given creature once every 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting, fear effect, though it can affect any creature with an Intelligence score regardless of immunity, in such a case the creature can only become shaken, not frightened. The martial master must have selected menacing skill focus technique to gain this technique.

Perfect Attack (Ex) (2 FP, 10th): The martial master can, expand Focus as a full-round action, make a single perfect attack). When they do, they make the attack against the target’s touch AC, and ignores all damage reduction. If this perfect attack is used in conjunction with menacing skill, menacing skill ignores the target’s immunities to mind-affecting or fear by nature of the stunning precision of the strike.

Press the Advantage (Ex) (1 FP, 6th): The martial master doubles the die of their melee weapon one step at the end of a charge, as the Vital Strike feat. This focus technique counts as Vital Strike for the purposes of feat prerequisites and if the martial master subsequently gains Improved Vital Strike or Greater Vital Strike, it applies to the charge as normal. However, any feat that uses this ability as a prerequisite may only be used in conjunction with this ability. This ability does stack with Vital Strike. If Focus points are required, it is per charge.

Returning Weapon (Su) (2 FR, 6th): The martial master has such mental control of their weapon that they can throw it and have it return to them, defying physics. To do so, the martial master expends Focus and makes a ranged attack, with a range increment of 20 feet. No penalties for improvised thrown weapons are imposed. At the end of the attack, the weapon returns.

As a full-round action, the martial master may target one additional target per 4 levels they have, who are no more than 30 feet apart. One attack roll is made and compared against the AC of each of the targets.

Skilled Parry and Riposte (Ex) (2 FP, 1st): When an opponent attempts an attack with a melee or ranged weapon against the martial master, the martial master can expend Focus and a use of an attack of opportunity to attempt to parry that attack. The martial master makes an attack roll as if they were making an attack of opportunity; for each size category the attacking creature is larger than the martial master, the martial master takes a -2 penalty on this roll. If the result is greater than the attacking creature’s result, the creature’s attack automatically misses. The martial master must declare the use of this ability after the creature’s attack is announced, but before the attack roll is made. Upon performing a successful parry, the martial master can, as an immediate action, make an attack against the creature whose attack they parried, provided that creature is within their reach or first range increment. Penalties to attack from Combat Expertise or fighting defensively do not apply to the parry attempt but do apply to the riposte.

Stowed Readiness (Ex) (1 FP, 2nd): The martial master is considered to be wielding their weapon for ability and feat purposes and threatening their normal area even when their weapon is not drawn. An attack of opportunity taken while the weapon is stowed is considered a drawing attack. This ability does not allow the martial master to threaten an area or make attacks of opportunity with weapons normally unable to do so, unless they have a focus technique like ammo threat (see page 4). If the expenditure of a Focus point is required, it is for each attack of opportunity and no additional FP is required for the drawing attack. The martial master must have the drawing attack focus technique before selecting this technique.

Study the Enemy (Ex) (2 FP, 4th): The martial master takes times to observe the movements and techniques of his opponent, looking for gaps in their defenses and skills. By expending Focus as a move action, the martial master can study a single enemy they can see. Upon doing so, they add 1/2 their martial master level as an insight bonus to attack and damage rolls against the creature. This benefit lasts for a number of rounds equal to the martial master’s Wisdom modifier. The martial master can choose to end the study bonus early to deliver extra precision damage. This precision damage starts as 1d6 and increases by 1d6 for every 4 levels the martial master possesses after 4th. In all cases, the bonus damage is precision damage and is not multiplied on a critical hit and is ineffective against creatures immune to precision damage.

If used with a ranged weapon, the creature must be within 30 feet. Also, if the target benefits from concealment, the martial master loses the insight bonus. The martial master can only have one target for this ability at a time.

Sure Grip (Ex) (1 FP, 1st): The martial master is immune to disarm, steal and sunder combat maneuvers made against a weapon they are wielding. If the expenditure of a Focus point is required, it is for each combat maneuver thwarted in this manner.

Targeted Attack (Ex) (1 FP, 8th): As a full-round action, the martial master can expend Focus, if applicable, to make a single attack and choose a part of the body of their target. If the attack hits, they gain the following effects depending on the part of the body targeted. If a creature does not have one of the listed body locations, that part cannot be targeted. Creatures that are immune to precision damage are immune to these effects.

Arms: The target takes no damage but drops one carried item of the martial master’s choice, even if the item is wielded with two hands. Items held in a locked gauntlet are not affected.
Head: The target is damaged normally and is also confused for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting effect.
Legs: The target is damaged normally and knocked prone. Creatures with four or more legs or those that are immune to trip attacks are immune to this effect.
Torso: The target is staggered for 1 round.
Wings: The target is damaged normally and must make a DC 20 Fly check or fall 20 feet.

Turn the Killing Blow (Ex) (2 FP, 10th): When hit by an attack that would reduce the martial master to 0 or lower or struck by a critical hit, the martial master may expend Focus as an immediate action. The martial master must make an attack roll. If the result of the attack roll exceeds the damage dealt, the martial master remains at 1 hit point or reduces the critical hit to normal damage. If the attempt fails, they are dealt damage as normal.

Will Over Magic (Su) (2 FP, 8th): The martial master can use their iron mind to use their weapon to deflect magic. The martial master can now use their skilled parry and riposte to parry and deflect magic attacks. If targeted by a melee or ranged touch attack from a spell, spell-like ability or supernatural ability, they may parry and riposte the attack as normal. Alternatively, if the attack is a ray, they may instead use their riposte to redirect the ray to another target within the spell’s range. In this case, the martial master rolls a touch attack against the new target but the spell gets its effects from the original caster. If the spell or effect is targeted (not area-of-effect) and requires a Reflex save, The martial master may roll an attack roll as if parrying an attack with skilled parry and riposte and use their parry result in place of their Reflex save. The martial master must have the skilled parry and riposte focus technique prior to acquiring this technique.
